arxiv-1910-11118.title: Shallow Art: Art Extension Through Simple Machine Learning
arxiv-1910-11118.creator: Kyle Robinson, Dan Brown
arxiv-1910-11118.description: Abstract Shallow Art presents, implements, and tests the use of simple single-output classification and regression models for the purpose of art generation. Various machine learning algorithms are trained on collections of computer generated images, artworks from Vincent van Gogh, and artworks from Rembrandt van Rijn.

arxiv-2101-05750.title: p p -adic dynamical systems of the function a ​ x − 2 ax^{-2}
arxiv-2101-05750.creator: U.A. Rozikov
arxiv-2101-05750.description: Abstract . In this paper we study p p -adic dynamical systems generated by the function f ⁡ ( x ) = a x 2 f(x)={a\over x^{2}} in the set of complex p p -adic numbers. We find an explicit formula for the n n -fold composition of f f for any n ≥ 1 n\geq 1 .

arxiv-2103-02722.title: A Markov jump process associated with the matrix-exponential distribution
arxiv-2103-02722.creator: Oscar Peralta
arxiv-2103-02722.description: Abstract Let f f be the density function associated to a matrix-exponential distribution of parameters ( 𝜶 , T , 𝒔 ) (\bm{\alpha},T,\bm{s}) . By exponentially tilting f f , we find a probabilistic interpretation which generalises the one associated to phase-type distributions.

arxiv-2112-01800.title: A Survey: Deep Learning for Hyperspectral Image Classification with Few Labeled Samples Journal: Neurocomputing
arxiv-2112-01800.creator: Sen Jia, Shuguo Jiang, Zhijie Lin, Nanying Li, Meng Xu, Shiqi Yu
arxiv-2112-01800.description: Abstract With the rapid development of deep learning technology and improvement in computing capability, deep learning has been widely used in the field of hyperspectral image (HSI) classification. In general, deep learning models often contain many trainable parameters and require a massive number of labeled samples to achieve optimal performance.

arxiv-2301-08935.title: Phonon-mediated dark to bright plasmon conversion
arxiv-2301-08935.creator: Benjamin Rousseaux, Yanko Todorov, Angela Vasanelli, Carlo Sirtori
arxiv-2301-08935.description: Abstract The optical response of a matter excitation embedded in nanophotonic devices is commonly described by the Drude-Lorentz model. Here, we demonstrate that this widely used approach fails in the case where quantum-confined plasmons of a two-dimensional electron gas interact strongly with optical phonons.

arxiv-2307-05062.title: System of Spheres-based Two Level Credibility-limited Revisions
arxiv-2307-05062.creator: Marco Garapa, Eduardo Fermé, Maurício D. L. Reis
arxiv-2307-05062.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Marco Garapa, Eduardo Fermé, Maurício D. L. Reis. Two level credibility-limited revision is a non-prioritized revision operation. When revising by a two level credibility-limited revision, two levels of credibility and one level of incredibility are considered. When revising by a sentence at the highest level of credibility, the operator behaves as a standard revision, if the sentence is at the second level of credibility, then the outcome of the revision process coincides with a standard contraction by the negation of that sentence.

arxiv-2311-00037.title: Complex orders and chirality in the classical Kitaev- 𝚪 \bm{\Gamma} model
arxiv-2311-00037.creator: P. Peter Stavropoulos, Yang Yang, Ioannis Rousochatzakis, Natalia B. Perkins
arxiv-2311-00037.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by P. Peter Stavropoulos, Yang Yang, Ioannis Rousochatzakis, Natalia B. Perkins. It is well-recognized that the low-energy physics of many Kitaev materials is governed by two dominant energy scales, the Ising-like Kitaev coupling K K and the symmetric off-diagonal Γ \Gamma coupling. An understanding of the interplay between these two scales is therefore the natural starting point toward a quantitative description that includes sub-dominant perturbations that are inevitably present in real materials.

arxiv-2410-01436.creator: Rafael Correa, Abderrahim Hantoute, Marco A. López
arxiv-2410-01436.description: Abstract This paper deals with the regularization of the sum of functions defined on a locally convex space through their closed-convex hulls in the bidual space. Different conditions guaranteeing that the closed-convex hull of the sum is the sum of the corresponding closed-convex hulls are provided.

arxiv-2505-19409.title: Fusion Intelligence for Digital Twinning AI Data Centers: A Synergistic GenAI-PhyAI Approach
arxiv-2505-19409.creator: Ruihang Wang, Minghao Li, Zhiwei Cao, Jimin Jia, Kyle Guan, and Yonggang Wen*
arxiv-2505-19409.description: Abstract The explosion in artificial intelligence (AI) applications is pushing the development of AI-dedicated data centers (AIDCs), creating management challenges that traditional methods and standalone AI solutions struggle to address. While digital twins are beneficial for AI-based design validation and operational optimization, current AI methods for their creation face limitations.

arxiv-2506-07632.description: Abstract The necessity of complex numbers in quantum mechanics has long been debated. This paper develops a real Kähler space formulation of quantum mechanics [ 19 ] , asserting equivalence to the standard complex Hilbert space framework. arxiv-2509-06445.title: Learning to detect continuous gravitational waves: an open data-analysis competition
arxiv-2509-06445.creator: R Tenorio, M J Williams, J Bayley, C Messenger, M Demkin, W Reade, Kaggle Competitors
arxiv-2509-06445.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by R Tenorio, M J Williams, J Bayley, C Messenger, M Demkin, W Reade, Kaggle Competitors. We report results of a public data-analysis challenge, hosted on the open data-science platform Kaggle, to detect simulated continuous gravitational-wave signals. These are weak signals from rapidly spinning neutron stars that remain undetected despite extensive searches. The competition dataset consisted of a population of CW signals using both simulated and real LIGO detector data matching the conditions of actual CW searches.

arxiv-2509-15038.title: Value-Guided KV Compression for LLMs via Approximated CUR Decomposition
arxiv-2509-15038.creator: Ayan Sengupta, Siddhant Chaudhary & Tanmoy ChakrabortyDepartment of Electrical EngineeringIndian Institute of Technology Delhi, India ayan.sengupta@ee.iitd.ac.in, urssidd@gmail.com, tanchak@iitd.ac.in
arxiv-2509-15038.description: Abstract Key-value (KV) cache compression has emerged as a critical technique for reducing the memory and latency overhead of autoregressive language models during inference. Prior approaches predominantly rely on query-key attention scores to rank and evict cached tokens, assuming that attention intensity correlates with semantic importance.

arxiv-2511-01599.title: Clutter Suppression in Bistatic ISAC with Joint Angle and Doppler Estimation
arxiv-2511-01599.creator: M. Ertug Pihtili, Julia Equi, Ossi Kaltiokallio, Jukka Talvitie, Elena Simona Lohan, Ertugrul Basar, and Mikko Valkama
arxiv-2511-01599.description: Abstract The coexistence of radar and communications in wireless systems marks a paradigm shift for the sixth-generation (6G) networks. As 6G systems are expected to operate at higher frequencies and employ larger antenna arrays than fifth-generation (5G) systems, they can also enable more accurate sensing capabilities.

plos-pbio-0000067.title: Distinct Mechanisms Determine Transposon Inheritance and Methylation via Small Interfering RNA and Histone Modification
plos-pbio-0000067.creator: Zachary Lippman, Bruce May, Cristy Yordan et al.
plos-pbio-0000067.description: PLOS ONE research article. Heritable, but reversible, changes in transposable element activity were first observed in maize by Barbara McClintock in the 1950s. More recently, transposon silencing has been associated with DNA methylation, histone H3 lysine-9 methylation (H3mK9), and RNA interference (RNAi).

pmc-11410995.title: Potential of kaempferol and caffeic acid to mitigate salinity stress and improving potato growth
pmc-11410995.creator: Musarrat Ramzan, Sakeena Tul Ain Haider, Muhammad Baqir Hussain, Abdullah Ehsan, Rahul Datta, Tahani Awad Alahmadi, Mohammad Javed Ansari, Sulaiman Ali Alharbi
pmc-11410995.description: Salinity stress adversely affects plant growth by disrupting water uptake, inducing ion toxicity, initiating osmotic stress, impairing growth, leaf scorching, and reducing crop yield. To mitigate this issue, the application of kaempferol (KP), caffeic acid (CA), and plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) emerges as a promising technology.

pmc-12502123.title: Abstracts from the 33rd Portuguese Dental Association Annual Meeting
pmc-12502123.creator: Unknown
pmc-12502123.description: and implementing new techniques, materials, and approaches to enhance the effectiveness of treatments. The use of micro-implants as temporary skeletal anchorage devices has become increasingly prevalent in modern orthodontics. However, placing micro-implants in the mandibular platform presents specific challenges, mainly due to the proximity to the mandibular canal.

pmc-12615368.title: Comparison of postoperative atrial fibrillation after total coronary revascularization via left anterior thoracotomy and conventional median sternotomy coronary artery bypass grafting
pmc-12615368.creator: Sefa Sural, Vedat Aslan, Deniz Mutlu, Nurettin Yeral, Ozerdem Ozcaliskan, Gokhan Gokaslan
pmc-12615368.description: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is the most common arrhythmia that occurs after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), contributing to increased mortality, morbidity, longer hospital stays, and higher healthcare costs. Total coronary revascularization via anterior thoracotomy (TCRAT) has recently emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to the traditional median sternotomy (MS).

pmc-13145808.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1528 INCIDENCE OF ANEURYSMAL SUBARACHNOID HEMORRHAGE BY AGE, SEX, REGION, AND TIME PERIOD IN KAZAKHSTAN: A NATIONAL COHORT STUDY
pmc-13145808.creator: Karashash Menlibayeva, Chingiz Nurimanov, Iroda Mammadinova, Lu Liu, Owase Jeelani, Serik Akshulakov, Yanzhong Wang
pmc-13145808.description: Background and aimsAneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) accounts for approximately 5% of all strokes and is associated with high morbidity and mortality. The global crude incidence is estimated at 7.9 per 100,000 person-years. Despite a worldwide decline in incidence, substantial regional variation persists, and data from Central Asia remain scarce.

pmc-13295952.title: Autologous Nanofat Indications in Wound Healing: A Systematic Review
pmc-13295952.creator: Stefanie Bonini, Patricia Fuentes, Richard Brannon Claytor
pmc-13295952.description: Introduction: Chronic wounds and pathologic scars remain a persistent challenge in plastic surgery. Conventional treatments can be costly and inconsistent, prompting interest in regenerative approaches that utilize autologous tissue. Emulsified fat produces nanofat through mechanical processing and contains adipose-derived stem cells, stromal vascular fractions, extracellular matrix proteins, cytokines and growth factors.

pmc-13338363.title: Structure-guided identification of small molecules potentially able to modulate GDF15 activity
pmc-13338363.creator: Antonio Chiariello, Lorenzo Lenti, Lorenzo Trofarello, Manuela Sollazzo, Mattia Lauriola, Alberto Del Rio, Stefano Salvioli, Marco Daniele Parenti, Maria Conte
pmc-13338363.description: Growth Differentiation Factor 15 (GDF15) has been associated with different pathological conditions, including cancer cachexia. Various strategies, such as monoclonal antibodies and peptide antagonists, have been developed to inhibit GDF15 activity; however, it is currently unknown whether using small organic molecules (SOMs) can effectively target GDF15.
